dct_description_sm: Berry picking is an important autumnal activity in northern communities providing a local and abundant source of nutrients. Berries are an important link in the food chain, but very little is known about potentially important insects for pollination and berry shrubs dependence on these insects. Insect life cycles strongly depend on temperature and synchrony between their emergence and flowering might be affected by increasing temperatures. On the other hand, under climate change scenarios, shifts in species range are predicted to increase the number and diversity of pollinators in the Arctic. In this context, this project aims to assess insect pollinator abundance at the time of flowering of berry shrubs and to determine their effect on blueberries production at Baker Lake, Nunavut.
dct_title_s: Impact of pollinators on berry productivity and the biodiversity of pollinating insects at Baker Lake, Nunavut
